chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Naḍr, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to perform ghusl with one sāʿ, and when one of his wives was with him, he would perform ghusl with one sāʿ and one mudd.

Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: the least amount of water that suffices in ghusl al-janābah is that which is like oil for the body, with which a person wipes himself in a state of necessity due to severe cold or scarcity of water. This indicates that.

key_terms.الضَّرُورَةِ: a state of necessity or hardship
key_terms.صَاعٍ: a sāʿ, a known measure used here for the amount of water
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: ritual bath required after the state of janābah
key_terms.مُدٍّ: a mudd, a smaller unit of measure added to the sāʿ
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلُ: performs ghusl, meaning ritual washing of the body

ai.seo_question: How much water is sufficient for ghusl al-janābah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the amount of water the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used for ghusl and indicates moderation in water usage during ritual purification. It also notes that in cases of necessity, such as severe cold or lack of water, a minimal amount sufficient to cover the body may suffice for ghusl al-janābah.
